description: Use this when the user wants a video clip made from a prompt; for a finished, branded video ad use render_ad. Render a RAW video clip from your own prompt and return its served mp4 URL. For finished brand ADS prefer render_ad (it runs the Studio quality pipeline — composited text, clean speech, end card, music); use this for raw/experimental clips or precise manual control. ONE generation = one continuous clip up to the model’s longest listed duration — the longest-clip model in the catalog today renders a full multi-beat spot of up to 30 SECONDS in ONE unbroken take with native synchronized audio, so never assume a generic 8–10s cap and never stitch something that fits one clip; durationSeconds must be one of the model’s durations from hermoso_capabilities, which is the live list. TO GET A SPECIFIC MODEL, NAME IT in `model`: an unnamed render is routed by the server’s own auto-pool, which is narrower than the catalog, so the longest-clip and highest-resolution models are reached by naming them. Renders take 1–3 min. refImage anchors the opening frame; ttsScript adds a voiceover. AUDIO IS NOT FREE AND NOT OPTIONAL BY DEFAULT: a clip delivered with no audio of its own gets a music bed composed and CHARGED on top of the render (see musicMood and audio) — on a cheap short draft the bed can cost as much as the clip. Pass refVideo (a clip URL) to EDIT an existing video instead — the omni engine transforms that clip per your prompt, inheriting its canvas + length (aspectRatio/durationSeconds are ignored for an edit). RAW MODEL ACCESS: by default a few small guards are appended (packaging/label safety with no reference image, a negative prompt where the model takes one, reference-binding lines) and hex colour codes become colour names; raw:true dispatches your prompt to the model BYTE-IDENTICAL — no rewriting, no appended guidance, no negative prompt, no brand references attached on your behalf. Credits, the durable delivery of the finished asset and the per-model validation are unchanged. Spends credits (Starter plan is video-blocked server-side).

angles.description: OPTIONAL, OFF BY DEFAULT: with `creator`, also send the extra views that creator already has saved (their pose plates, up to 2) beside their portrait. A test showed no visible improvement over the portrait alone, and each extra view adds about 25 s before the render starts, so leave it off unless asked. Views are skipped when the face library is busy, and the render always goes ahead on the portrait.

audio.description: default true. false = render SILENT: no native model audio, no music bed, and no bed charge held or billed. This is the ONLY way to decline the automatic bed (see musicMood) — leave it alone for anything that should have sound, and do not combine it with ttsScript.

cameraMove.description: A named camera move around the still in refImage (orbit = a quarter turn, the default; orbit_half / orbit_full = a half turn / a turntable). Only minimax-h3-max-camera renders one: with model omitted it is picked; any other named model is refused, nothing charged. Needs refImage.

cameraTrajectory.description: Your own ordered camera path, 2 to 12 keyframes, for the camera-controls model only (same rule as cameraMove; overrides it). The first pose is held until its time and the last pose is held to the end. A value outside these bounds is refused by name, nothing charged.

azimuth.description: horizontal angle around the subject in degrees (0 = where the still was taken; the sign turns the camera the other way; at most 32 full turns of total travel)

distance.description: distance from the subject in scene units, 1 = the distance of the still; smaller is closer

elevation.description: vertical angle in degrees, -90 (below) to 90 (straight above)

time.description: when this pose is reached, 0 = start of the clip, 1 = end

creator.description: STAR A SAVED CREATOR in this clip — their id from list_creators, or the name you know them by, or a PRESET AI creator from list_creators presets (exact name or id; free, no generation). Their saved portrait rides first among the references as the on-camera person, with their saved consent, exactly as render_ad casts them; a real person saved from a photo keeps their real face on camera. An unknown name is refused by name, nothing charged.

durationSeconds.description: length of THIS ONE clip in seconds: one of the CHOSEN model’s listed durations in hermoso_capabilities (they differ per model, 4–8s on the short ones up to 30s). One continuous generation, so a longer ask than the model’s longest clip is REFUSED, nothing charged (never quietly truncated). Past ~15s NAME a long-clip model in `model`. For a longer spot use plan_ad with durationSeconds then render_ad, which stitches acts (on a 15s model, 40s = 15+15+10).

endImage.description: local path or URL of the LAST frame: the clip travels from refImage (required with it) to this image. Only models with endFrame true in hermoso_capabilities take it; any other named model is refused by name, nothing charged.

extend.description: true = EXTEND refVideo by durationSeconds (default 5) with what your prompt says happens next, as ONE clip. By default it CUTS to a NEW SHOT: new angle, same scene, room sound carried, no music at the cut. A named model (any i2v) renders it.

extendMode.description: with extend: 'continue' = the SAME take past its last frame, only when asked seamless (models with extend in hermoso_capabilities).

faceRoute.description: 'face_lane' records the user's statement "I own the rights to this face" for the real person in their reference (paid plans; the likeness terms apply). Set it only when the user picked that option after a render said it could not use that face, and send the same request again; it then renders through Hermoso's face library at the normal price. Never set it on your own. The other options are a different `model` or one of the user's saved `creator`s.

interactionId.description: with extend:true on an Omni model: the interactionId returned by an earlier render on that model — continues it from its own stored context instead of re-uploading refVideo.

loop.description: true = a seamless loop whose last frame flows back into its first. Only models with loop true in hermoso_capabilities; needs refImage and cannot be combined with endImage.

model.description: video model id from hermoso_capabilities; a named model is never swapped without asking. Omit to let the router pick; its default per job (jobEngines in hermoso_capabilities, from watched side-by-side tests) is seedance-2.5 for product, lifestyle, a person talking to camera and 30s single takes (cheaper engines broke the product there). A model the user picks is kept; never switch it

musicMood.description: the mood of the music bed (upbeat / calm / warm / epic / tense / playful / elegant / hype / chill / dramatic; default warm). It does not decide WHETHER there is one: a clip with no audio track (a "silent" model in hermoso_capabilities, or one that came back mute) gets a bed composed and CHARGED automatically at explainerMusicCredits. audio:false = silent, no bed, no charge.

prompt.description: the video prompt / shot description (for a refVideo edit, this is the transformation instruction); optional with `shots`

raw.description: Send the prompt to the model exactly as written, without the wording Hermoso usually adds (packaging and label guidance, reference lines, colour names for hex codes, quality hints). Use it when you want the model's own interpretation rather than Hermoso's render craft. Two vendor-required fixes still apply: extra @ImageN tokens are dropped and an over-long prompt is trimmed at a sentence (on Veo it is refused with the length and the cap instead). Billing, durable delivery and per-model validation are unchanged.

refImage.description: local path or URL to anchor the first frame. Using a real person’s face, likeness or voice confirms you are them or have their consent, take full, unlimited responsibility for its use and will cover any claim against Hermoso (hermoso.ai/terms). Paid plan only; recorded.

refImages.description: SEVERAL reference images (paths or URLs: a person, products, a place) that must all appear. A model uses up to its `refs.max` in hermoso_capabilities (one-image models take the first); with `refs.promptAddressed`, name them Image 1, Image 2… in order. minimax-h3-max-ref takes 9 and keeps each as a reference, not a first frame.

refVideo.description: URL of an existing video to EDIT rather than generate from scratch — the clip is transformed per your prompt, keeping the SOURCE clip’s aspect ratio and, on models hermoso_capabilities marks `sourceLength`, its LENGTH (their `durations` are the per-second price ladder; a durationSeconds sent is reported as unused). Trim the source to change the length. Omit `model` for the default editor, or name a model whose videoEdit is true in hermoso_capabilities (a named model that cannot edit is refused, nothing charged); refImage rides along as the look of what the edit adds. With extend:true this is instead the clip to EXTEND. Omit to generate a fresh clip.

resolution.description: '1080p' default; '480p'/'720p' cheaper drafts, '4k' premium (more credits). A model renders only the tiers in its own `resolutions` list in hermoso_capabilities; a tier it lacks renders at its best one without a word, so check before promising 1080p or 4k.

shots.description: MULTI-SHOT: one clip cut into these shots, in order; the seconds add up to a length the model renders. Replaces `prompt`. Only models with multiShot true in hermoso_capabilities; a shot prompt over that model’s shotPromptMaxChars (Kling 3.0: 512) is refused free, never cut.

seconds.description: this shot’s length in whole seconds

speak.description: A PERSON SAYING THESE EXACT WORDS TO CAMERA — the default for any "make my photo talk" / spokesperson / talk-to-camera ask. Pass with `creator` or a portrait as `refImage`: the video model films them saying it in their own voice, matched to who they are, and the length follows the words (leave durationSeconds out). `prompt` is then the staging (e.g. "natural", "walking in a park"). Real footage, not an animated photo; generate_avatar is the animated-photo look, only when asked for by name

name: generate_video
title: Generate video
